Le Centre de Recherche en Technologies I: The Center for Research in Industrial Technologies (CRTI) has just obtained the first national accreditation for drone pilot training, marking a key milestone in strengthening technological skills in Algeria. This certification, issued by the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, positions Algeria as an emerging player in the industrial drone ecosystem.
Une première nationale dans un secteur e: A national first in a rapidly expanding sector
Le Centre de Recherche en Technologies I: The Center for Research in Industrial Technologies (CRTI), based in Algiers, has officially obtained the first national accreditation for drone pilot training, according to a press release from the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research published on June 4, 2026. This certification, issued via its specialized subsidiary EPE CRTI SKY-TEC, covers classes 1 and 2 of drones, thus addressing industrial and professional uses.
Cette accréditation s’inscrit dans une d: This accreditation is part of a broader momentum to strengthen national capabilities in advanced technologies, as Algeria accelerates its digital and industrial transition. CRTI, a public institution under the supervision of the ministry, thus becomes the first Algerian entity authorized to train drone pilots according to national standards, in response to the growing needs of the energy, agricultural, logistics, and security sectors.
Une réponse aux enjeux industriels et éc: A response to industrial and economic challenges
L’obtention de cette accréditation inter: Obtaining this accreditation comes at a time when drones are playing an increasingly strategic role in the Algerian economy. Industrial applications, such as the inspection of oil and gas infrastructure (where Sonatrach and its partners operate), agricultural surveillance (particularly for large cereal farms in the South), or even the mapping of mining areas, require certified skills.
Le CRTI, en collaboration avec des acteu: CRTI, in collaboration with stakeholders such as the National Agency for the Valorization of Research Results (ANVREDET) and industrial partners, has established training programs aligned with international standards while incorporating the specificities of the Algerian market. These training courses, accessible to companies, public institutions, and individuals, aim to bridge the gap between supply and demand for technological skills.
Cette avancée s’ajoute à d’autres initia: This breakthrough adds to other recent initiatives aimed at structuring the drone sector in Algeria. In 2025, the government had already launched a national plan for drone development, including subsidies for equipment acquisition and training. Furthermore, local startups, such as Drone Algeria and SkyTech Solutions, are beginning to emerge, although the market is still dominated by international players.
Pour les opérateurs télécoms algériens (: For Algerian telecom operators (Mobilis, Djezzy, Ooredoo), this accreditation opens up prospects in terms of connectivity and drone-associated services. Indeed, industrial drones require stable and secure networks for real-time data transfer, which could stimulate technological partnerships in the coming years.
Si cette accréditation constitue une ava: While this accreditation represents a major breakthrough, several challenges remain:
La standardisation des formations : Assu: Training standardization: Ensuring program consistency to avoid disparities between approved centers.
L’adaptation aux besoins sectoriels : Dé: Adapting to sector-specific needs: Developing specialized modules for key industries (energy, agriculture, construction).
La sensibilisation des entreprises : Con: Raising awareness among businesses: Convincing economic players of the usefulness of drones, particularly in a context of high initial costs.
Le CRTI, en tant que pionnier, a désorma: CRTI, as a pioneer, now has the responsibility to unite stakeholders and position Algeria as a regional hub for drone training. This ambition is in line with the government's vision of making technological innovation a lever for economic growth.
Pour aller plus loin : Le ministère de l: Going further: The Ministry of Higher Education has announced that the first training sessions will begin as early as September 2026, with limited places to ensure educational quality.
